title: Brouwer OQ-02 Extensions: Contraction Uniqueness and Error Bounds
description: Proves contraction mapping uniqueness, a priori error bound |x − x*| ≤ ε/(1−L), geometric convergence of iterates, and 1D Sperner's lemma (combinatorial backbone of Brouwer). 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The Banach fixed-point theorem gives O(log 1/ε) iterations for contractions. Error bounds and stability results quantify the PPAD-complexity perspective on approximate Brouwer fixed points.
overview.problemStatement: Prove uniqueness, error bounds, geometric convergence for contractions, and 1D Sperner's lemma as combinatorial backbone.
overview.proofStrategy: Uniqueness: |x-y| = |f(x)-f(y)| ≤ L|x-y| < |x-y| → contradiction. Error: |x-x*| ≤ |x-f(x)|/(1-L) ≤ ε/(1-L). Convergence: geometric ratio L^n. 1D Sperner: any walk from 0 to 1 must have odd crossings.
keyInsights: **A priori bound**: |x - x*| ≤ ε/(1-L) for ε-approximate fixed points gives the key estimate — to achieve precision δ, approximate f within δ(1-L).
**Geometric convergence**: n iterations give error ≤ L^n·|x₀-x*|. The number of iterations is O(log(1/ε)/log(1/L)) = O(log 1/ε) since L < 1 is fixed.
**1D Sperner**: any 2-coloring of the path 0,1,...,n with color 0 at 0 and color 1 at n has an odd number of color-changing edges — the 1D case of Sperner's lemma.

sections.title: Contraction Uniqueness, Error Bounds, and 1D Sperner
sections.mathContext: $|x - x^*| \leq \varepsilon/(1-L)$ for $\varepsilon$-approximate fixed points; $1$D Sperner: odd color-changes.

conclusion.summary: 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Contraction uniqueness, error bounds, convergence, and 1D Sperner proved.
conclusion.implications: These results justify the O(log 1/ε) PPAD complexity for finding approximate contraction fixed points.
openQuestions: Can the Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration be proved to converge for non-expansive maps?
Can the PPAD hardness of approximate Brouwer be reduced to this quantitative analysis?
Can Kakutani's fixed-point theorem (for set-valued maps) be proved in Lean?
